## Four potato cups

Take four peeled potato halves and scoop each one out to make a cup. Make one cup from a boiled potato. Stand each cup in a beaker of water. Cup A stays empty, B gets a teaspoon of sugar, C a teaspoon of salt, and the boiled cup D a teaspoon of sugar.

<!-- STEP -->
## Two hours later

Press **Wait 2 hours**. Water gathers in the hollows of cups B and C. Water from the beaker has moved through the potato towards the sugar or salt, by osmosis.

<!-- STEP -->
## Why cup A matters

Cup A has nothing in its hollow, and no water gathers. It shows what happens with no sugar or salt, so we can be sure that the sugar or salt made the difference in B and C. An experiment needs a comparison like this.

<!-- STEP -->
## Why the boiled cup fails

Cup D has sugar and yet no water gathers. Boiling leaves its cells dead, so their membranes no longer work as selectively permeable membranes, and osmosis does not take place.
